edits.target: Of every $100 charged, how much is left after cost?
edits.new_value: Read these as three separate measurements, not one firm at three nested boundaries. The top bar is a share of API list price for an OpenAI and Anthropic blend. The middle bar is Anthropic's margin on the revenue it actually collects: SemiAnalysis puts the blended price customers really pay for Opus 4.7 near $0.99 per million tokens, against a $5/$25 sticker. The bottom bar is OpenAI's whole-company margin on all revenue, about 70% of which is ChatGPT subscriptions rather than metered answers. So the fall in height is not the boundary effect at work. Widen the boundary around Anthropic and you do not arrive at 42.6. The top two 80% ranges also overlap almost fully, 52 to 94 against 55 to 82, so the step from 85 to 72 is not a gap this evidence can settle. All three stay positive, so US labs charge more than the direct cost of an answer (T2). The deeper reason the numbers differ: the top bar is a MARGINAL cost — one more answer on a machine that is already busy. The bottom bar is closer to an AVERAGE cost — the whole rented fleet divided by the answers it actually served, including the machines sitting idle and the free users who pay nothing. A lab rents capacity, not tokens, so most of its cost does not shrink when it sells fewer tokens. That is why a fat margin on one paid token and a thin margin on the whole firm are both true at once.
edits.why: Deletes the two sentences that claimed the descent was a nesting effect ('the wider you draw the cost boundary, the thinner the margin gets') and replaces them with what the three bars actually measure, naming each firm and each base. Adds the overlap check on the top two intervals, which the chart already draws (52-94 vs 55-82, straight from the spec), so the reader is not sold a step the evidence cannot resolve. The marginal-vs-average paragraph is kept verbatim: it is correct and is the chart's real payload. All figures are existing spec or claim values ($0.99/M and $5/$25 from mc-09's notes; 70% from rv-06). FK 8.7, ease 63.4, fog 10.7, SMOG 11.1.

edits.target: Does the whole build pay? Three scenarios
edits.new_value: One project: every US AI dollar from 2024 out past 2030, plus a tail — one lumped estimate for all the years after 2030. Future dollars are discounted, meaning marked back to what they are worth today; the total is the net present value. Each case is priced at its own cost of capital, 8.5% to 11%, because the world where the build disappoints is also the world where money costs more. That gap does real work: the base case turns negative if you charge it the bear's 11%. Two of three cases clear the bar — but the base case clears by only $487B, and the drop from base to bear ($2.8T) is six times the climb to bull ($420B). Every year through 2030 loses cash, so all the payoff waits for the years after 2030: strip them out and even the bull case loses $3.3T. The hinge is the mature margin — the cents of each sales dollar the industry keeps once it has stopped growing. About 5c either way moves the base case roughly $0.5T and can flip its sign. Its clock is chip life: a frontier chip serves about 3.9 years (dp-10), yet CoreWeave re-signed expiring H100s at about 95% of the old price (dp-09). Figures from the P1 total-program DCF (discounted cash flow) model; not an externally graded claim.
edits.why: Removes the literally false "discounted at a 9-10% cost of capital" and states what actually matters: the base model's own sensitivity says "At 11% ... NPV turns negative", so the choice of rate moves the answer, not just the modelling. Also carries four jargon glosses at their first use on the page — the tail (a lumped estimate for the years after 2030), discounted (marked back to today's money), net present value, and mature margin (the cents kept once growth stops) — plus the DCF expansion, which lands before visual 9's "Valuation (DCF)" dot. All figures ($487B, $2.8T, $420B, $3.3T, 3.9 years, 95%, 8.5/9.5/11%) already exist in the spec or forecasts.json. FK 8.68 / ease 73.1 / fog 11.69 / SMOG 10.13.
